questions.prompt: You swap the embedding model behind an existing index. What has to change?
questions.explanation: Vectors from different models live in different spaces: re-embed everything, expect a possible dimension change, and re-tune any similarity thresholds. Chunk boundaries are independent of the model.

options.body: Every stored vector must be re-embedded
Nothing, if both models are from the same vendor

questions.prompt: Cosine similarity and dot product rank results identically when...
questions.explanation: On unit-normalised vectors, the dot product equals the cosine.

questions.prompt: Which are typical causes of poor recall from a dense retriever?
questions.explanation: Domain shift, rare exact-match terms (IDs, codes), and asymmetric query/passage encoding without the right prefixes all hurt recall.

options.body: Domain shift from the model's training data

questions.explanation: Matryoshka training makes leading sub-vectors usable on their own, so you can truncate dimensions for cost.

options.body: truncate to fewer dimensions with graceful quality loss
store several resolutions from one model

questions.prompt: Is `<script>alert(1)</script>` shown as text, not executed, when a prompt is rendered?
questions.explanation: Prompts are Markdown rendered without raw HTML, so inline code and stray tags are plain text.

options.body: Yes, inline code is rendered as literal text

questions.prompt: A prompt contains a raw tag outside code: Does it become an element?
questions.explanation: Without rehype-raw, raw HTML is not parsed into elements; it is shown as text.

options.body: No, it is rendered as text
Yes, an image element is created
